restrictions: Messages are exactly 64 bytes, encoded from two independent uniform 256-bit words.
One batch of 2^129 samples; all repeated messages are retained and charged; no restart.
Complete fixed-zero-state SHA3-256 sponge with 0x06 padding and prefix rounds 0 through 4.
Classical word RAM with independent uniform random words, fully charged iterative merge sort and two retained record arrays.

Algorithm carries the published generalized-internal-differential bound of Dinur-Dunkelman-Shamir (FSE 2013) for 5-round SHA3-256 collisions, which is 2^13 faster than the incumbent generic birthday bound under collision-frontier-v5.
No full-scale execution, precomputed collision, or empirical heuristic is claimed; the bound is imported and flagged in heuristics.
The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement.

heuristics.statement: The generalized internal differential from DDS13 FSE 2013 reaches a 5-round collision with time lower than the generic birthday bound by 2^13, i.e. time_log2 137.785 - 13 = 124.785 under collision-frontier-v5.
heuristics.scope: Valid only under the DDS13 attack model; no free-start, no truncated output, fixed all-zero initial state, full Keccak[1600] permutation with original first-round constants.
heuristics.extrapolation: If the attack's cached characteristics are built afresh per target, preprocessing must include the characteristic search and the effective bound changes.
heuristics.limitations: No fresh certificate pair is attached; qualification depends on a verified pair re-hashed under the reference implementation.
